# T6.14: HEVC Main 10 (10-bit)

Since every app gets our encoder (T6.13), an app asking for HEVC Main 10 got 8-bit, and Parsec with "prefer 10-bit
color" fell back to Apple's software encoder (it sets `ProfileLevel = HEVC_Main10_AutoLevel` and drops a session that
refuses it): L 60-130 ms at 4K. Now `libnvencvt` encodes real 10-bit: **Parsec 10-bit at 4K, L 7.0-7.3 ms**.

## How it was found (runtime observation, option B)

`vttest` got `VT_10BIT=1` (x420 input with detail below one 8-bit step, ProfileLevel Main10, decoded and compared at
10 bits) and `VT_L10R=1`. nullmoth's `libnvenc_hevc` (registered with `trace/nmreg.c`) encodes Main 10 on Ada; traced
with `trace/nvtrace.c` at 256x128, 8-bit and 10-bit (`docs/traces/main10/`: logs, streams, picture setups).

The tracer needed two fixes for driver 2.3.6:
- **GPU addresses are per client.** The encoder library and NVK in the same process each have an RM client, and their
  GPFIFOs sit at the same GPU address (0x200090000). The poller looked addresses up without the client and followed
  NVK's queue: no NVENC submissions seen. Lookups now prefer the followed channel's client.
- **Mappings end with `IOServiceClose`** (`nvrm_xnu_munmap`): the tracer kept the CPU address and the poller faulted on
  unmapped memory. `IOServiceClose` / `IOConnectUnmapMemory64` / `NV_ESC_RM_UNMAP_MEMORY` now drop it.

## 8-bit vs 10-bit picture setup (nullmoth's)

| field | 8-bit | 10-bit |
|---|---|---|
| `sps_data.bit_depth_minus_8` | 0 | 2 |
| `pps_data.transform_skip_enabled_flag` | 1 | 0 |
| `pps_data` reserved1 (byte 7, bit 3) | 0 | 1 (meaning unknown) |
| `rate_control.minQP[0..2]` | 0 | -12 (QP range grows by 6 x (bit depth - 8)) |
| setup reserved word at 0x314 | 0x0999 | 0x0222 (meaning unknown; we leave 0 in 8-bit) |
| ref/output `luma_bot_offset` / `chroma_bot_offset` | 64 / 32 | 128 / 64 (planes in bytes double) |
| surface `sfc_pitch` fields | 256 | 256: **in samples**, not bytes |

No pushed method changes. Input and reference planes hold 16-bit samples (chroma at +2 x the 8-bit luma size; reference
slots 0x28000 apart at 256x128, the 8-bit rule "planes + 64 KB"). Headers: `general_profile_idc` 2, compatibility flags
0x20000000, `bit_depth_luma/chroma_minus8` 2, transform skip off.

**Input samples: P010 as CoreVideo has them** (10 bits in the high bits of each 16-bit sample), in the 8-bit input
layout with twice the bytes per row. Low-bit alignment gives garbage (5.7 dB).

## Parsec sends l10r

With Main 10 accepted, Parsec still showed L 31-130 ms while our encoder took 5.7 ms: VideoToolbox converted every frame
from Parsec's format to our x420 on its serial preparation queue (`VTMetalTransferSessionTransferImageSync` through
nullmoth's Metal plugin: surface-in upload, `waitUntilCompleted`), and frames queued behind it (L = 1-2 frame periods). A
diagnostic switch (`/tmp/nvencvt.anyfmt`: offer every candidate format, log what comes) showed **l10r**
(`kCVPixelFormatType_ARGB2101010LEPacked`, ScreenCaptureKit's 10-bit RGB). A Main 10 session now takes l10r and converts
it in the tiling pass (`nvenc_in_tile_l10r`: BT.709 video range, 16.16 fixed point, 2x2 chroma average, AVX2 build where
available, 4 threads): **4K 3.2-3.9 ms**, entry to emit 7.2 ms.

The coefficients match VideoToolbox's transfer to 1 code value on test colours. Its chroma is point-sampled (the top-left
pixel of each 2x2: 68 dB against that, 43 dB against our average), so `VT_L10R` reports ~43 dB chroma for us; luma
61.6 dB.

## Results (VideoToolbox, `vttest`, decoded by Apple's software decoder, PSNR at 10 bits)

| input | size | result |
|---|---|---|
| x420 | 640x360, 1280x720, 1920x1080 (120 frames), 3840x2026, 3840x2160 | 0 decode errors, 62.2 / 61.2 / 56.9 / 48.2 / 49.7 dB at 20 Mbit/s |
| x420 | Apple's software encoder, 256x128 | 58.4 dB (ours 63.0) |
| l10r | 1920x1080 | luma 61.6 dB vs Apple's conversion |
| x420 / l10r | 4K timing | engine 4.4-4.8 ms as 8-bit; tiling 2.0 ms (x420) / 3.2-3.9 ms (l10r), 8-bit 1.1 ms |

Also new: `/tmp/nvencvt.log` writes the encoder log (every property set, first frame format) to
`/tmp/nvencvt-<pid>.log` in apps started by launchd.
